newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening lower Wednesday as gold weakened overnight to fresh 4-1/4 year lows due to fresh short positions put on by funds this week, dealers said.
The white metals were also weaker on news that Russia would begin its delayed 1997 exports on July 10.
COMEX August gold was called to open $1.75 to $2.50 an ounce weaker from Tuesday's close at $335.10 an ounce. London bullion was fixed at $331.45 an ounce, down from $333.70 on Tuesday afternoon.
Bullion was quoted by dealers at $331.50/$332.00.
On ACCESS August gold was down $2.70 at $332.40 an ounce, traded $335.50 to $332.40.
September COMEX silver was called to open 1.5 to 2.5 cents weaker from Tuesday's close at $4.678 an ounce.
COMEX gold stocks were up 5,246 ounces at 850,240 ounces Wednesday, while COMEX silver stocks fell 837,789 ounces to 184,691,207 ounces.

NYMEX October platinum was seen opening down $3.00 to $4.00 an ounce from the previous close at $411.90, while NYMEX September palladium was expected to open off $1.00 to $2.00 an ounce from $176.30 at the close Tuesday.

Russia's platinum group metals export agency on Wednesday informed Japanese clients by fax that Russia would resume PGM shipments to Japan around July 10, Japanese precious metals traders said overnight.
